description: The shared secret-name rule marks these members because their names contain `password`, `secret`, `token`, `credential` or `encryption key`, but each one is not a secret: it holds the name of a Secret Manager secret or version, a Cloud KMS key, a Credential resource, or a Cloud Storage URI of an encrypted file, so the secret itself is never in the field; or it is an opaque id with no access attached: a page, partition, sequence, consistency or stream position, an attribution or logging id, an execution-name suffix, a model token's text or a media fingerprint. This removes the mark.
